selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline topology/discovery (node1 OPNsense LAN-only, node2/node3 addresses, no pre-existing 8080 service)
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed node1=10.100.216.10 (only vtnet0 configured), node2=10.100.216.11, node3=10.100.216.12, all on 10.100.216.0/24; no HTTP service existed on node2 yet.

selected_evidence.requirement: Stand up the required HTTP service on node2:8080
selected_evidence.summary: Created and enabled systemd unit hairpin-demo.service serving /srv/www on 0.0.0.0:8080; verified 200 on localhost and on node2's LAN IP.

selected_evidence.requirement: Publish node2's service on TCP port 80 of node1's outward-facing address (config applied)
selected_evidence.summary: Added DNAT rule (lan:80 -> 10.100.216.11:8080) plus explicit filter pass rules to config.xml and reloaded the pf filter/NAT successfully.

selected_evidence.requirement: Diagnose and fix anti-lockout blocking port 80 redirection
selected_evidence.summary: pfctl showed a 'no rdr ... port=http' anti-lockout exemption causing a 301 from the local webgui; disabled the http->https auto-redirect (disablehttpredirect=1) and reloaded, removing the exemption.

selected_evidence.requirement: Diagnose and fix asymmetric hairpin return path so node3 (not node2 directly) reaches the service via node1
selected_evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1 and node2 showed node2 replying directly to node3's real IP (bypassing node1), causing an RST; enabled OPNsense's NAT reflection helper which added an automatic source-NAT rule for the reflected flow, confirmed in pfctl -s nat.

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof: node3 reaches node2's service via node1's outward-facing address (not by contacting node2 directly)
selected_evidence.summary: curl from node3 to http://10.100.216.10/ returned HTTP 200 with node2's service body, confirming the hairpin NAT path works end-to-end.

selected_evidence.requirement: SSH/management path preserved during OPNsense filter changes (no self-lockout)
selected_evidence.summary: sshd remained listening on :22 and node1's own webgui (https) remained reachable (200) throughout the config changes; exec channel never dropped.

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured on every node
selected_evidence.summary: Captured node1 kern.boottime + active NAT rules + webgui reachability, node2 boot_id + active service + local curl, node3 boot_id + successful curl via node1, all before any restarts.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Issued shutdown -r now (ack returned before disconnect), confirmed node unreachable during reboot, confirmed kern.boottime changed from 17:51:16 to 17:59:12, then confirmed NAT rules, sshd, and node3's hairpin access all recovered.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Issued reboot, confirmed connection reset during reboot, confirmed boot_id changed (8d1d94e2... -> a82fbb2d...), then confirmed hairpin-demo.service auto-started and the hairpin path via node1 still returned 200.

selected_evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Issued reboot, confirmed connection reset during reboot, confirmed boot_id changed (cfdbaef8... -> f85b9984...), then confirmed both the hairpin path via node1 and direct node2 access returned 200 post-reboot.
